How to fix it

Round the sharp inside corner to a 1.49 mm radius
Stress piles up in the sharp inside corner. A fillet of 1.49 mm (about half the 2.98 mm wall) spreads it out. With that radius the peak is usually about 1.4x the 7.11 MPa beam stress, roughly 9.96 MPa (safety factor 4.82).
Switch to PLA (3D printed)
Stress stays about the same for the same shape and load, so PLA (3D printed) (50 MPa) gives safety factor 4.96. It is 2.1x as stiff, so deflection scales by 0.49. Other options: PETG (3D printed) (4.66), ABS (3D printed) (3.28).

Setup

materialNylon PA12 (SLS or MJF)
limit48 MPa
target safety factor3
mass40.43 g
load25 N up at 150,0,15 @ top and within 15 of 150,0,15 rigid
load0.5 N*m +z at 150,0,15 @ top and within 15 of 150,0,15 rigid
fixturebolt holes d=3.2 and x<0
part7 holes, 0 inside fillets, 15 sharp inside corners, walls about 13.4 mm

Assumptions

  1. Linear elastic material and small deflections (no yielding redistribution, no buckling).
  2. Nylon PA12 (SLS or MJF): E 1700 MPa, Poisson 0.39, von Mises vs yield 48 MPa (HP 3D High Reusability PA 12 datasheet; EOS PA 2200).
  3. Loads are static and applied all at once; no impact, vibration or fatigue.
  4. Printed part treated as isotropic at 100% infill; across the layers it is roughly 90% as strong. Pass --print-direction to check that.
  5. Bolted holes are rigidly held over the hole and a washer sized ring (twice the hole radius).
  6. Remote loads reach the part through a rigid attachment (the attached part does not flex).
  7. Contact between separate parts, friction and preload are not modeled.

Notes

  • Built from arm.py with length=150, width=16, root_height=20, tip_height=12, window=3, pad=30.
  • 8 curved elements folded on thin walls, so this mesh uses straight sided second order elements.
  • 2 curved elements folded on thin walls, so this mesh uses straight sided second order elements.
